_README: The benchmark roster: which models we owe runs for.
CONSTRAINT: every entry in `roster` must be lane=local — a model that runs on our own
hardware. Remote/paid models live in `special_occasions` and are run rarely and
deliberately. Enforced by `bench_scoreboard.py --self-test`, which `just check` runs.
PROVENANCE: this file is INTENT, not record. The record is bench-results.jsonl, which is
append-only and never edited. A model removed from `roster` keeps every published row,
because the scoreboard is built from results first and the roster only adds queued rows.
Removals are still written down in `retired` with a date and a reason — an eviction with

hardware.name: NVIDIA DGX Spark
hardware.note: Personal box; every local-lane number is measured here and should be disclosed as such. Unified memory means nothing is memory-constrained — even a 120B at Q4 fits. Bandwidth is the binding constraint, so generation speed tracks bytes streamed per token: MoE beats dense at equal total size, and a lower quant roughly halves the bytes. Plan instance budgets from measured tokens/sec, never from parameter count.

constraint.why: The claim is that the harness earns its place on hardware we own. A roster that quietly mixes in frontier API models measures something else, and the mixed table is not readable as either result.

roster.isolates: the incumbent — bound scoreboard rows already exist; known conformance=no_tools
purpose-built agentic coder — the fairest test of whether the machinery adds value or compensates
competent native tool calling; the mid-point of the conformance range
NVIDIA lineage at matched size; A3B MoE, so likely the FASTEST here and the right iteration model
IBM lineage — guards against a result that is really a Qwen/Mistral/NVIDIA monoculture artifact
weak-model control: the harness advantage should be LARGEST here, and it is cheapest to iterate on
strong-model control: does the advantage shrink as capability rises? A12B, so cheaper per token than '120B' suggests

special_occasions._why: Paid/remote models. Tokens are Shawn's, so these run rarely and on purpose — a release, a claim worth checking against a frontier reference, or a result that looks too good. They are NOT part of the regular rotation and must never enter `roster`; their numbers are a reference point, not an own-hardware result, and must be labelled as such.

retired._why: Removed from the active rotation. Their published results STAND — bench-results.jsonl is untouched and the scoreboard still renders them, because it is built from results first. This section exists so the decision to stop running them is itself provenanced.
